feature: Any colour for an arrow, with chip words that stay readable
summary: A picked arrow or measurement has a Color row with eight swatches and a Custom well. Any colour retints the line, the head and the label chip at once, and every chip style picks its own plate and words so the label reads, with no trip into Advanced.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no switch changed from its default.

try.do: Open any screenshot, press A, drag an arrow and type a label, then press Command Return.
try.shotNote: The window was photographed behind another app, so it shows the window's background look (picked controls read grey).

try.do: In Appearance, click the Custom well at the end of the Color row and type a light green, 7FD18B, in HEX.
Click through the ten Chip tiles and read the label on each.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Pick a dark indigo, 3A2E8F, in the same well and click through the tiles again.
Change the picture to black (or open a dark screenshot) and read the Glass chip again.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Paint Label Text by hand in a blue close to the chip (4A90E2) and read the line under the Color row.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Click Reset Colors under that line.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

evaluate: Does every chip stay readable for any colour you pick, on a white, a black and a busy picture?
Is it clear that the last well in the Color row is where any other colour comes from?
Does the head change with the line the way you expect, and stay put when you had painted it apart?
Is Reset Colors the words you would look for to undo a hand-painted label that went unreadable?
rough: A new arrow is drawn in the tool's red (#FF3B30), which is not one of the design system's eight (its red is #FF375F), so on a fresh arrow the Custom well is the one lit and the row reads Color #FF3B30. Logged on this task; the arrow tool's default ink is the Appearance task's call (arrow-and-measurement-appearance-shows-only-styl).

Measurements have the same Color row, warning and Reset Colors since 2026-11-01 (every-measurement-wears-the-same-chip-styles-col); the walk below picks colours on an arrow only, the measurement chip is read by the same pixel reader in its own walks.

any-colour-chip-reads-walk now runs by pointer press (2026-11-01, after a-walk-s-press-on-a-picture-tile-swatch-or-colou): light green 7FD18B and indigo 3A2E8F, all ten chip styles, read off the real window over white, black and a busy photo. Worst 4.68:1 (Hairline plate in light green); Glass 4.83:1 over black and 7.70:1 over white in indigo, 9.12 to 13.31 in light green.
Glass in indigo over pure black is the closest call at 4.83:1: readable, but only just above the 4.8 the design system aims for.
